title: Burst recovery latency diagnosis and quick-run logs
quick_summary: Small, focused scratchpad capturing repeated short-burst traffic tests against the local dev cluster. Goal: understand why p99 balloons for 30–90s after a 30s spike despite KV cache hit rate staying relatively high. Running lightweight probes (1-node dev net) to capture timeline and stack traces; next step is a full Dedicated repro.
body:
Context:
- Observed in integration: sudden customer traffic burst -> app sees p99 jump 6x for ~1 minute and errors on some requests. Hypothesis: KV cache/eviction + background recompile/quantization path + cold threads. Want to isolate which component (runtime scheduling, kernel warmup, cache miss storms, GC-like uplifts) is dominant.

Test harness (local dev cluster):
- 1 x a10g-equivalent node (dev image), serving 7B llama variant (qat quantized int8), patched kernel selection debug prints enabled.
- Model pinned to v2-quant-low-bw.
- Prefix KV caching enabled; cache size configured to hold ~10k sidecar keys.
- Batching: continuous-batch enabled, target batch 8, max batch latency 30ms.
- Load generator: wrk-style custom driver producing Poisson arrivals with configurable mean QPS and instantaneous ramp to burst QPS.
- Instrumentation: p50/p90/p95/p99 latencies, CPU/GPU utilization, KV cache hit/miss counters, scheduler queue depth, kernel switch logs. Traces collected with trace-id in header.

Traffic pattern used in these runs:
- Baseline steady: 30 qps for 3m to settle caches.
- Burst-up: jump to 220 qps for 30s.
- Post-burst: drop back to 30 qps and observe for 5m.
- Repeats: 6 iterations with 2m idle between repeats.

Representative run logs (timestamps relative to run start):
- 00:00 - baseline 30 qps: p50=18ms, p95=60ms, p99=120ms, KV hit=96%
- 02:00 - burst start -> 220 qps: immediate throughput ramp up; p50=28ms, p95=120ms, p99=650ms, error rate=0.2% (timeouts at 1s)
- 02:12 - p99 peak observed: 1.2s (several outliers to 2s), CPU spike on host + short GPU kernel queue backlog logged
- 02:30 - burst end -> traffic drops to 30 qps: p50 quickly returns to ~20ms, but p99 remains elevated at ~400–600ms for ~45s
- 03:15 - p99 back to baseline ~120ms; KV cache hit still ~94–96% throughout
- Notes: many p99 samples correlate with "kernel selection fallback" log lines and "scheduler thread steal" events.

Small ascii timeline (p99 ms):
[00:00]--------120---------| burst |---650-----450----120---
           baseline            30s spike  recovery  back-to-baseline

Deep-dive observations:
- KV cache hit rate barely drops (~96% -> 94%) so full cache miss storm unlikely to be the single cause.
- Kernel switch messages (runtime selected optimized kernel X, then fell back to generic Y) spike during burst and early recovery; fallback increases per-token processing time by ~3–6x. Suspect cold kernel caches on GPU and JIT-ish fallback.
- Scheduler queue depth jumps during burst; some batches are split (continuation batches) which create extra KV lookups and contention.
- A small fraction (~0.2–0.5%) of requests hit a code path that triggers a heavier quantized path recompilation (logged as "quant-profile-refresh"); these correlate with the highest tail samples.
- CPU side: short-lived high sys CPU (~60–80%) during burst, implying background housekeeping (e.g., memory compaction, cache eviction callbacks).

Quick experiment variants tried during the session:
- Variant A: increased batch max latency to 60ms -> slightly smoother p95, but p99 tail still present (peak ~850ms).
- Variant B: pre-warm kernel cache (fire synthetic empty inferences on kernels) before burst -> p99 peak reduced by ~30%, recovery faster (~25s).
- Variant C: disable continuous-batch -> throughput suffers but p99 tails shrink; indicates batching policy contributes to contention under burst.
- Variant D: force KV cache read-through prefetch for keys likely to be touched in the burst -> small improvement, but not sufficient.

Preliminary interpretation:
- Root cause appears to be a combination: kernel cache coldness (warming kernels costs many ms per token) + batching/scheduling contention that amplifies tail by creating hotspots which trigger heavier code paths (quant-profile-refresh). KV cache is not the main culprit although it contributes some.
- The long recovery window (~30–90s) likely due to a few components warming sequentially (kernel cache -> quant profile -> scheduler backpressure) rather than a single all-or-nothing event.

Immediate next steps (small, local):
1) Add targeted kernel pre-warm step in warmup flow (script to run representative ops for each model flavor).
2) Add metrics for "kernel cache size" and more granular timing around kernel selection to pinpoint expensive fallbacks.
3) Re-run Variant B with increased iterations and capture GPU kernel load traces.
4) Try a modified batching policy: cap batch size under burst (adaptive cap) to measure effect.

Action items (short):
- [ ] Add kernel pre-warm script to dev harness (Hao)
- [ ] Open perf ticket linking traces and logs (PERF-621) (Hao -> set up epics)
- [ ] Prototype adaptive-batch cap (Evan)
- [ ] Get SRE to run a Dedicated-scale repro with realistic customer traffic (Lena / infra)

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Which component is dominant at scale? (need dedicated cluster run)
- Can we push kernel warmup into model onboarding pipeline so production never sees cold kernels?
- Is quant-profile-refresh avoidable or can it be made async/non-blocking?

Notes-to-self: keep iterations short and instrument more during the first 60s after burst end. Capture a full heap+stack dump for a hotspot sample. Save a copy of kernel logs for comparison across model variants.
experiment_runs:
run-2026-03-02-01: baseline 3m, burst 30s, post 5m; p99 peak 1.2s; recovery 75s
run-2026-03-02-02: with pre-warm; p99 peak 0.8s; recovery 25s
run-2026-03-03-01: disable continuous-batch; throughput down ~18%, p99 peak 0.5s, but unacceptable throughput
run-2026-03-04-01: increase batch latency max to 60ms; p95 improved but p99 similar
